This full-day tour takes visitors to two iconic San Francisco Bay islands starting Saturday, May 30, 2026 from 9:40 am to 1:35 pm (approximately 5½ hours). The tour departs from Alcatraz Landing at Pier 33 in San Francisco and includes round-trip ferry rides to both islands, an award-winning cellhouse audio tour on Alcatraz where you can explore the historic prison that housed notorious criminals, and a one-hour narrated tram tour of Angel Island. Angel Island, known as the "Ellis Island of the West," offers breathtaking views of the Bay while learning about its history as a major immigration hub from 1910-1940s. The event runs from 10:30 AM to 11:30 AM. Graduate students from Cal State East Bay's LISTEN with AAC training program conduct the sessions, demonstrating language use on AAC devices while developing a love for reading. The program is designed for emergent communicators four years old and up—including both new and existing AAC users who typically communicate with single words—and is open to children of all abilities. A parent or caregiver must accompany the child, with limited seating of one caregiver per child. The program accommodates the slower pace of AAC communication. For questions or accommodations, contact Polina at prubanova@aclibrary.org or 510-745-1464.

events.title: Native Intertribal Dance + Food Fest at The Presidio (Tunnel Tops)
events.description: Day of dance, music, screen printing, arts and crafts marketplace, health screenings, and more by the Native American Health Center.
events.event_detail: Native Intertribal Dance + Food Fest at The Presidio (Tunnel Tops) is a free outdoor community event held on Saturday, May 30, 2026, from 11:00 am to 4:00 pm at Tunnel Tops in the Presidio (603 Mason St., San Francisco, CA 94129). Organized by the Native American Health Center, this event welcomes indigenous communities and the greater public for a day celebrating Native American culture through dance, music, screen printing, an arts and crafts marketplace, and health screenings. Dance is described as a prayer and offering in many indigenous communities, serving to balance physical, mental, spiritual, and emotional selves while healing and strengthening communities. Attendees can bring their own picnic or purchase food from Presidio Pop Up's food and beverage vendors. The event is family-friendly and free to attend.

events.title: They Called Us Enemy Book Discussion
events.description: Join us for a discussion of They Called Us Enemy, a graphic memoir by actor and activist George Takei. He recounts his childhood imprisoned in American incarceration camps during World War II.
events.event_detail: They Called Us Enemy Book Discussion is a library event hosted at the Albany branch of Alameda County Library. The event takes place from 11:00 AM to 12:00 PM and has already occurred. Attendees participate in a discussion of the graphic memoir 'They Called Us Enemy' by actor and activist George Takei, which recounts his childhood imprisoned in American incarceration camps during World War II. The book explores themes of patriotism, family, loyalty, and what it means to be an American. This event is suitable for adults, teens, and seniors. Library staff may be present to take photos or recordings. ASL interpretation or closed captioning can be provided if requested at least seven days in advance.

events.title: Family Movie Matinee Pop-Up
events.description: Come join us at the Lakeview branch with the whole family and enjoy a movie!
events.event_detail: Come join the Lakeview Branch of Oakland Public Library for a family movie matinee! Bring the whole family to watch a movie together at this free community event. The pop-up screenings happen on select Saturday mornings from 11:00 AM to 1:00 PM, with upcoming dates including January 31st, March 28th, May 30th, and September 26th. Families can enjoy a film in the library's community space while meeting neighbors and enjoying quality time together. No registration required. Suitable for all ages.

events.title: Drawing From Film: La Llorona (2019) in SF
events.description: Free drawing from film event featuring La Llorona (2019).
events.event_detail: Drawing From Film workshop at San Francisco Main Public Library where participants watch Jayro Bustamante's political folk horror film La Llorona (2019) and draw striking frames during pauses. This self-led event has no instruction or feedback, but offers an opportunity at the end to view others' drawings and share your own. Basic materials (pencils, paper, erasers) are provided, though you may bring your own. Watercolor, ink, and gouache are permitted, but no fume-creating paint or paint pens. The film runs 96 minutes with English closed captions and subtitles. Due to pauses for drawing, the full film will not be shown. Free event. Takes place in the Latino/Hispanic Meeting Room on the Lower Level.

events.title: Bayview Family Festival
events.description: Family-friendly festival event
events.event_detail: Bayview Family Festival is a free family festival held at India Basin Waterfront Park in San Francisco on Saturday, May 30 from 11 AM to 2 PM. The event features inclusive activities and food for all families, with special welcome for families of children with disabilities and complex medical needs. The festival is presented by Support for Families of Children with Disabilities in partnership with Wu Yee Children's Services, with support from the San Francisco Department of Early Childhood. Attendees can expect a variety of family-friendly activities, food vendors, and community resources in a waterfront park setting. The event runs for 3 hours in person.

events.title: How to Find Peace After Estrangement (Even if Nothing Changes)
events.description: Wellness workshop on finding peace after family estrangement
events.event_detail: A free 1-hour online workshop titled 'How to Find Peace After Estrangement (Even if Nothing Changes)' hosted by Andrea Beck Coaching. This event is designed for parents struggling with estrangement from their children who experience constant emotional pain, guilt, confusion, and exhaustion. Attendees will learn why estrangement creates an emotional spiral, what's keeping them stuck, and how to find peace even if the relationship hasn't changed. The workshop focuses on helping participants feel stable, clear, and at peace—not on fixing the child. Multiple dates available, with the next session on Saturday, May 30 at 11 AM MST. Participants do not need to talk or participate if they prefer not to. This is an online event held via video conference.

events.title: Paws to Read - Saturday
events.description: Would your child like to read to a friendly therapy dog? Children in grades K through 5 can read to dogs certified for sociability. Beginning readers can get low-stress practice, fluid readers can make a new furry friend.
events.event_detail: Paws to Read is a reading program where children in grades K through 5 can read aloud to friendly therapy dogs certified for sociability. This 15-minute session provides beginning readers with low-stress practice and allows confident readers to make new furry friends. The event takes place on Saturday, May 30, 2026, from 11:00am to 11:15am at the Orinda Library branch, located at 26 Orinda Way, Orinda, CA 94563. Attendees are asked to arrive five minutes before their allotted time and check in with program staff. The event is part of the Contra Costa County Library system and is specifically designed for children ages 6 to 12 and tweens. No registration or fee is required to participate.

events.title: Lakeshore Spring Festival
events.description: Lakeshore Spring Festival
events.event_detail: The Lakeshore Spring Festival is a free, family-friendly celebration of Oakland's Lakeshore District happening on Saturday, May 30th, 2026 from 11AM to 7PM at Lakeshore Avenue and Lake Park Avenue. This inaugural festival marks over a decade since the award-winning district has hosted a festival, celebrating the area home to the Oakland LGBTQ Center and newly commemorated Lakeshore LGBTQ Cultural District. The event features two stages of live music including DJ JOJO, Osada 3, La Gente SF, Rumbaché, Jafin, and The Futurelics Fashion Show curated by Meeka Star, plus a 90's Dance Party. Families can enjoy a kid's zone, artisan market, craft cocktails, and local craft beers. Master of Ceremonies is Candi Martinez. Admission is free and all ages are welcome.

events.title: Excelsior Cleanup w/ Free Food & Drink For Volunteers (SF)
events.description: Community cleanup event with free food and refreshments for volunteers.
events.event_detail: Volunteer neighborhood cleanup event in San Francisco's Excelsior/Mission District area. Meet at Recovery Room (4528 Mission St) to get supplies and form teams. Cleaning runs from 11:00am to 12:00pm around the neighborhood. Afterwards, enjoy free food and refreshments. Organized by Civic Joy Fund and Refuse Refuse. Free to participate, but registration is required via their Mobilize page. Great opportunity to help beautify the community while meeting neighbors and earning free food.

Co-hosted by Sutter Health-CPMC Inpatient Rehabilitation and BORP, this event invites people of all experience levels and disabilities to learn about and try adaptive cycling, adaptive pickleball, and wheelchair basketball. All adaptive equipment is provided. Attendees can explore new adaptive activities, connect with community resources, and enjoy complimentary pizza and snacks.

Participants also get the opportunity to practice a mock interview, which simulates the actual citizenship interview process. Free study materials are provided. The class is bilingual, offered in both English and Spanish, making it accessible to a diverse community. This event is suitable for adults (19+).

events.event_detail: Maker Exploration is a hands-on maker event at San Mateo County Libraries offering guided experiences with 3D printers and laser cutters. Participants can learn Tinkercad for 3D printing (with a 20-minute print limit) and use a Glowforge laser cutter to create a personalized acrylic charm (2" square size limit). The event runs from 11:00 AM to 1:00 PM and is suitable for children ages 6-11 and teens ages 12-18. Maker volunteers provide hands-on guidance throughout the session. Drop-ins are welcome as space and time allow. This event has already occurred and was held at the Foster City library branch.

events.title: Free Fun on the Farm, Saturday's, San Ramon
events.description: Fun on the Farm Activities is FREE crafts and activities that highlight farm life and the late Victorian era. These Saturday events are an opportunity to step back into history and enjoy the simple things of life.
events.event_detail: Free Fun on the Farm is a free Saturday event held from 11 AM to 2 PM at Forrest Home Farms (19953 San Ramon Blvd., San Ramon). This is a partnership between the City of San Ramon and the San Ramon Historic Foundation featuring free crafts and activities that highlight farm life and the late Victorian era. It's an opportunity to step back into history and enjoy simple things of life. The event rotates activities each week - for example, the May 30th event features "Tea Traditions" celebrating Ruth Boone with afternoon tea, learning about tea traditions, and making a tea craft to take home. Most activities are free, though special fee-based fundraising programs may require registration.

events.title: Stitches of Resilience: Origami Bag Sewing Project
events.description: Join Katie Furukawa Bonifacio of Old River Design Co. for a hands-on workshop that explores the intersection of heritage and craft.
events.event_detail: Join Katie Furukawa Bonifacio of Old River Design Co. for a hands-on workshop exploring heritage and craft. Participants use Japanese fabrics and origami-inspired folding techniques to sew a unique carry-all shoulder bag. The workshop is inspired by George Takei's 'They Called Us Enemy' and includes reflections on the facilitator's family incarceration experience, turning sewing into a space for storytelling, remembrance, and honoring sacrifices. Participants must know basic machine sewing (zig-zag stitch, forward, reverse), but no additional experience is required. The event runs from 11:00 AM to 1:30 PM at the Woodside branch of San Mateo County Libraries and is part of the One Book, One Coast series. Suitable for teens ages 12-18. Participants can expect to learn origami-style bag construction while engaging in meaningful conversation about Japanese American history.

events.title: Analogue Amalgamation
events.description: A group show exploring the art studio as both a workspace and listening room, where music operates as a quiet but persistent force in structuring time, guiding movement, and influencing decisions.

The exhibition runs from April 25 through May 30, with an opening reception on Saturday, April 25 from 5:00 pm to 9:00 pm. Regular gallery hours are Wednesday through Friday, 11:00 am to 5:00 pm, and Saturday, 12:00 pm to 5:00 pm. Over 40 participating artists display original artworks paired with vinyl records curated by Tunnel Records across six musical genres: rock, reggae, soul, hip-hop, jazz, and Latin. The venue transforms into part gallery, part record store—all analog. Attendees can view artwork, browse vinyl selections, and experience how sound operates as an active presence in visual art. Admission is free.

events.title: Chinese Medicine for Chronic Pain
events.description: According to the CDC, in 2023, 24.3% of adults had chronic pain. Dr. Julia Lee will discuss natural reasons why the body manifests pain, what the healing process for pain may look like, and strategies to cope with pain.
events.event_detail: A health lecture by Dr. Julia Lee, a licensed acupuncturist and diplomate of Oriental Medicine, discussing Chinese medicine approaches to chronic pain. According to CDC data, 24.3% of adults had chronic pain in 2023. Dr. Lee explains natural reasons the body manifests pain, the healing process, coping strategies, and beneficial attitudes for pain relief. She covers common pain areas (knee, lower back, shoulder, neck, headache) from the perspective of meridians and organ connections. This talk is suitable for adults, older adults, and caregivers/family members of those with chronic pain. Attendees can expect live music and DJ sets, performers, hands-on art-making activities, light bites, wine, and a community exhibition showcasing 100+ East Bay Open Studios artists including OAM's newest Emerging Artists cohort. Guest jurors will select and announce award winners, and art raffle tickets will be available. The exhibition continues Sunday, May 31, 12pm-4pm. events.title: Kintsukuroi Movie Screening
events.description: KINTSUKUROI is the Japanese art of repairing pottery using urushi lacquer and gold. It shows us that something shattered can be restored and made stronger and more beautiful.
events.event_detail: Kintsukuroi Movie Screening is a documentary screening at Campbell Library from 11:00 AM to 2:00 PM. The film "Kintsukuroi" (meaning "golden repair" in Japanese) is about the Japanese art of repairing pottery with gold, and tells the powerful story of Japanese American families who had their lives destroyed when President Roosevelt ordered the internment of 120,000 Japanese Americans at the start of World War II. The documentary follows these families from the prison camps of the American West to the battlefields of Europe. After the screening, there will be a Q&A session with the cast and crew. This event is part of Santa Clara County's Asian American, Native Hawaiian, and Pacific Islander (AANHPI) Heritage Month celebration and the One Book, One Coast program, which connects readers along the West Coast through literature. Suitable for adults and older adults. Free event at the library.

events.event_detail: Zither Celebration: Asian Identity Through Music is a concert event celebrating the zither as a symbol of Asian American identity and cultural survival. Taking place on Saturday, May 30, 2026 from 7:00 pm to 9:00 pm at the Oakland Asian Cultural Center (388 9th Street, Oakland, CA), the event features accomplished musicians Shirley Muramoto and Winnie Wong performing on the koto and guzheng. Through the luminous sounds of these traditional Asian string instruments, the program explores how cultural access is preservation and survival, especially in relation to Japanese American incarceration history and the ongoing shaping of Asian American identity. Though visually similar, the koto and guzheng carry distinct cultural lineages, each echoing stories of endurance, adaptation, and belonging. In this concert, they meet in collaboration and creative reimagining, bridging past and present, individuality and shared experience. The event uses a sliding scale payment model ($0-$35).

events.title: Irish Hurling & Gaelic Football Finals in San Francisco (Treasure Island)

events.event_detail: The San Francisco GAA St. Patrick's Cup Finals is one of the Bay Area's most unique sporting events, held on Sunday, May 31, 2026 from 9:30 am to 5:30 pm at Páirc na nGael on Treasure Island (13th Street and Avenue E). The event features the fast-paced Irish sports of Gaelic football and hurling. Gaelic football combines elements of soccer, rugby, and basketball with players kicking, passing, and battling for points. Hurling, often called the fastest sport on grass, features high-speed action and incredible skill. San Francisco is home to some of the top hurling clubs in the United States. The finals feature men's and women's championship matches, an energetic Irish sporting community, food and drinks, and family-friendly fun. Whether you have Irish roots or are discovering Gaelic games for the first time, this is a rare opportunity to experience Ireland's national sports in the Bay Area. Admission is $10 (cash only) with plenty of free street parking available.

The event runs on Sunday, May 31, 2026, from 9:30 AM to 3:00 PM. Participants must be 16 years or older and registration is required. Participants can expect hands-on exploration of owl pellets, learning to identify animal bones and understand food chains. This family-friendly activity combines science education with natural discovery, suitable for children and adults interested in wildlife.

events.title: Mental Health First Aid Training
events.description: Most of us would know how to help if we saw someone having a heart attack—we'd start CPR, or at the very least, call 9-1-1. Would you know how to respond if you saw someone having a panic attack or if you were concerned that a friend or colleague was developing a mental illness?
events.event_detail: Mental Health First Aid Training is an 8-hour certification course held at Millbrae Library. The training takes place across two sessions: May 30 from 10:00 AM to 2:00 PM in the Library Lounge, and May 31 from 10:00 AM to 2:00 PM in the Makerspace. Participants learn the Mental Health First Aid Action Plan and work through multiple scenarios to help someone in distress. The course teaches how to safely identify and address mental health and substance use concerns, improving understanding and confidence in starting important conversations. Attendees will receive certification upon completing both sessions and gain tools to support community members and loved ones. Registration is required, and participants must attend both days to become certified. This is an educational workshop suitable for adults (19+) focused on health, wellness, and life skills development.

events.event_detail: Join Call of the Sea for a free dockside tour of the Bay Area's own tall ship, the Matthew Turner. This 132-foot wooden brigantine was built in Sausalito, CA by the nonprofit Call of the Sea, launched in 2017, and has been sailing the Bay since 2020. It serves as an educational platform for students of all ages in seamanship, marine science, nautical history, and team building. The event takes place at the Richmond Ferry Terminal, 1453 Harbour Way, Richmond, CA. Free admission, but RSVP is required in advance. Tour runs Sunday May 31, 2026 from 10:00 am to 3:00 pm. The event runs from 10:15am to 11:15am and is led by Outdoor Yoga SF instructors. Participants can expect an all-levels vinyasa flow class with sweeping views of the San Francisco skyline and the Bay. The class costs $15 with advance registration recommended, and limited spots are available each week. Attendees should bring their own personal mat and dress in layers as the weather can be cool. Restrooms are available on site and there is ample parking. After class, visitors can stay to explore the waterfront paths, grab coffee or brunch, or enjoy the views from the island. The venue is accessible via a ferry from the San Francisco Ferry Building, taking just eight minutes.

events.title: Origami Workshop: Wishes
events.description: Explore the art of origami while reflecting on history and the human experience. In this hands-on workshop, participants will learn to fold a traditional origami crane, a symbol of hope, peace, and resilience.

The event runs from 10:30 AM to 12:30 PM and is part of the One Book, One Coast series. Participants will explore the art of origami while learning to fold a traditional origami crane, a symbol of hope, peace, and resilience. The workshop encourages reflection on history and the human experience, particularly Japanese American history connected to World War II experiences of being uprooted, separated from loved ones, and facing uncertainty. Attendees will connect historical perspectives to present-day events while creating their origami crane. This program is intended for adults (18+) and is 55+ friendly. Due to high demand, participants are asked to sign up for only one occurrence so more community members can participate. Materials are provided by the library.

events.event_detail: Explore Modern Thrillers: Cults + Corruption is a free author panel discussion part of the 2026 Bay Area Book Festival. Taking place Sunday, May 31, 2026 from 11:00 am to 12:00 pm at The Marsh in Berkeley, this event features authors Sarah Gailey, Jendia Gammon, Luke Goebel, and Paddy Hirsch exploring conspiracy, cults, and corruption in modern thriller fiction. The discussion covers themes of closed communities promising salvation, corporations concealing truths, and individual grief fueling public violence. The event is free to attend.

The YouthLit Corner offers family-friendly activities led by the Social Justice Children's Book Fair and ArtEsteem. The event welcomes all ages.

events.title: Just Dance Academy Spring Performance 2026
events.description: Just Dance Academy for their annual spring performance! A joyful afternoon of dance for the family!

The performance opens with JDA's beautiful rendition of the classical ballet Cinderella, followed by energetic and inspiring jazz, hip hop, and contemporary dance routines. This is a joyful afternoon and evening of dance suitable for the entire family. Admission is $40 for adults and $35 for children 12 and under. Free parking is available in lots adjacent to the theater.

events.title: Deep Healing and the Coming Transformation of Human Consciousness
events.description: Exploring the Forces Changing What it Means to Be Human: Michael Lerner and host Katherine Fulton
events.event_detail: The New School at Commonweal presents Deep Healing and the Coming Transformation of Human Consciousness with Michael Lerner and host Katherine Fulton on Sunday, May 31, 2026 from 1:00 pm to 3:00 pm, followed by a book launch reception from 3:00 pm to 4:00 pm. The event takes place at Gallery Commonweal (2nd floor, 451 Mesa Rd., Bolinas, CA 94924) or via Zoom. This is part of Commonweal's 50th anniversary celebrations and explores Michael Lerner's vision of healing ourselves and healing the earth, examining what he calls the coming revolution in human consciousness and what it means for individuals, communities, and as a planetary species. Lerner brings together over 230 week-long Cancer Help Programs, Healing Circles, and experiences with personal healing, in light of new research on consciousness. The event celebrates the publication of What Matters Now: 7 Letters to a Friend with Cancer. $25 suggested donation, no one turned away. Note: venue is on 2nd floor with no elevator.

events.event_detail: Drop-In 3D Printing is a free library program where participants can learn the complete 3D printing process from start to finish. The event takes place from 1:00 PM to 2:30 PM at the North Fair Oaks branch of San Mateo County Libraries. No registration is required, making it easy for anyone to drop in and participate. This hands-on workshop covers topics related to 3D design, printing technology, and the workflow involved in creating 3D printed objects. The program is suitable for all ages including children (6-11), teens (12-18), and adults (19+). It falls under categories of Art & Creativity, Technology & Innovation, and STEAM. Instruction is available in both English and Spanish. Attendees can expect a welcoming, educational environment where library staff guide them through operating 3D printers and understanding the technology.

Attendees can enjoy gardening and nature activities, carnival games, face painting, and arts and crafts. Live music will be provided by DJ KG. Families can stroll through the Green Between/Portola Garden, participate in story time with San Francisco Public Library, practice bike skills with SF Bike Coalition, and learn about the Portola neighborhood with PNA. events.title: San Francisco Youth Leadership Exposition
events.description: Youth leadership development event
events.event_detail: The SF Youth Leadership Expo is a Bay Area gathering bringing together student leaders, changemakers, and builders for a day of learning, networking, and skill-building. The event takes place on Sunday, May 31st from 1 PM to 5 PM (doors at 12:30 PM) at SPUR Urban Center San Francisco, located at 654 Mission Street in San Francisco, CA 94105. Through keynote conversations, practical workshops, networking sessions, and a youth organization expo, attendees will gain actionable insights on leadership, organization-building, outreach, advocacy, fundraising, social media growth, and creating meaningful community impact. Featured speakers include San Francisco Board of Supervisors President Rafael Mandelman, TikTok's Lead Product Manager Amar Saurabh, Enterprise for Youth CEO Carlo Solis, UC Berkeley Haas Interim Director Asra Khan, content creator Viraj Ala, and startup founder Alex Barra. Workshops include Social Media for Youth Organizations and Funding Basics. Free refreshments, networking opportunities, community tabling, and a matcha bar will be available throughout the event. Dress code is business casual. Attendees can expect to connect with ambitious young leaders from across the Bay Area, discover new opportunities, and strengthen skills needed to turn ideas into lasting impact.

This iconic event features the Godfather of Skate with his mobile DJ unit playing groovy tunes. Attendees can skate to the music, learn choreographed roller disco dance moves from experienced skaters, and enjoy the vibrant community atmosphere. The venue is officially dedicated as the home for outdoor roller skating in San Francisco. Skaters of all skill levels are welcome, with opportunities for beginners to learn and experienced skaters to show off their moves.

events.description: Cal Sailing Club Open House
events.event_detail: Cal Sailing Club Open House offers FREE introductory sailboat rides to the general public aboard a fleet of keelboats and dinghies. Open houses run from 1-3 pm on select Sundays throughout 2026 (April 5, May 31, June 28, August 2, August 30, October 4) plus May 2 during Berkeley Bay Fest. Boat rides are first-come, first-served; sign up in front of the clubhouse between 1-2:30 pm. Children must be at least 5 years old and accompanied by an adult. The club recommends first-timers and families with small children sail in larger, more stable keelboats. Participants can borrow foulies (raincoats) and life jackets at the club. Wear shoes that can get wet and comfortable clothes including a windbreaker. Bring a change of clothes as you may get soaked. The event takes place at Cal Sailing Club, 124 University Ave, Berkeley CA.

events.title: The Asian Art Museum presents: The Language of Flowers in Asian Art
events.description: Our Woven Heritage: Celebrating Asian American, Native Hawaiian, and Pacific Islanders: This May, we are celebrating AANHPI Heritage by highlighting textiles and clothing, and their importance as a method for sharing stories.
events.event_detail: The Asian Art Museum presents: The Language of Flowers in Asian Art is an educational presentation exploring the symbolic meaning of flowers in Asian art and culture. Discover how flowers like lotus, plum blossom, cherry blossom, chrysanthemum, tulip, and rose convey powerful messages in art. The event features objects from the Asian Art Museum's permanent collection and is part of the Asian American, Native Hawaiian and Pacific Islander Heritage Celebration. No registration required. Runs from 1:00 PM to 2:00 PM at the Corte Madera branch of Marin County Free Library. Recommended for 4th grade and up, suitable for adults, teens, and tweens. Attendees can expect to learn about the historical and cultural significance of flowers across various Asian traditions through this engaging presentation.

events.title: Tiburon Pride Picnic 2026
events.description: Laid-back, family-friendly waterfront picnic with views of the Golden Gate Bridge.
events.event_detail: Tiburon Pride Picnic 2026 is a free, family-friendly outdoor Pride celebration taking place on Sunday, May 31, 2026, from 1:00 pm to 4:00 pm at Shoreline Park in Tiburon. The event features stunning views of the Golden Gate Bridge and San Francisco skyline. Attendees can expect a relaxed picnic atmosphere with blankets on the grass, good music from DJ Kirill, fun activities, tarot readings by Sean Anomie, and vintage finds from Disco Dacha. The event celebrates the LGBTQ+ community in a beautiful waterfront setting with an open-air gathering. Bring your friends, family, and favorite picnic setup - or just come as you are. This is a free community event welcoming everyone to celebrate Pride together.

Suitable for all ages including children (6-11), teens (12-18), and adults. Participants can expect to design, build, solve creative problems, and practice repair techniques in a collaborative environment. The program is bilingual in English and Español.

It takes place on Sunday, May 31, 2026, from 1:00 pm to 4:00 pm at Mission St. and 20th St. in San Francisco's Mission District. This grassroots event aims to introduce Americans to better mangoes and offers attendees a chance to enjoy fresh mangoes while listening to DJ music in an outdoor park setting. The event is free and open to the public.

events.title: Embroidery on Clothing
events.description: Customize your clothing with embroidery in this hands-on workshop.
events.event_detail: Embroidery on Clothing is a hands-on workshop taking place at Mystic in Mill Valley, CA on Sunday, May 31, 2026 from 1:00 pm to 4:00 pm. Participants learn techniques for embellishing their own clothing with embroidery to personalize their style. You can choose from stick-on wash-off templates or design your own pattern. The workshop costs $65 per person and covers how to stabilize and hoop fabric, design transfer methods, and tools of the trade. Attendees need to bring a clothing item to embroider, preferably made of natural fibers like cotton, denim, or linen. Polyester and slippery, stretchy, or fuzzy materials are not recommended. A backup clothing option is suggested in case your primary item isn't suitable.

events.title: Watercolor in the Nectar Garden

Participants will learn watercolor painting techniques while surrounded by beautiful native California plants and flowers in the garden setting. The event appears to take place in the Regional Parks Botanic Garden, which is known for its diverse collection of California native plants and provides an inspiring natural backdrop for watercolor painting. Participants can expect to create their own watercolor artwork while enjoying the peaceful garden environment. The event focuses on connecting art with nature.

The event takes place from 1:00 PM to 2:00 PM at the San Carlos branch of San Mateo County Libraries. Attendees can learn new board games, challenge friends, or meet new people. This drop-in program is open to all ages and skill levels, including preschoolers, children, teens, and adults. No registration is required to attend this casual, welcoming library event.

events.title: Mottainai - Rope Bowl Making Class
events.description: Explore the intersection of craft and history through the lens of mottainai—the Japanese philosophy of respect and waste-reduction.
events.event_detail: Mottainai - Rope Bowl Making Class is a craft workshop exploring the Japanese philosophy of mottainai (respect and waste-reduction). This mindset helped Japanese Americans during WWII incarceration camps turn limited resources into handmade necessities. Instructor Katie Furukawa Bonifacio guides participants through sewing their own rope bowl using beautiful Japanese scrap fabrics while sharing reflections on her family's incarceration experience. The event connects to George Takei's 'They Called Us Enemy' and is part of the One Book, One Coast community reading event. Suitable for teens ages 12-18. Takes place from 1:00 PM to 2:30 PM at the Belmont branch of San Mateo County Libraries. Participants will learn basic sewing techniques while exploring themes of resilience and resourcefulness from Japanese American history.

events.title: Alice & the Wave Band Pop Music Concert (SF)
events.description: Pop music concert featuring Alice and the Wave Band.
events.event_detail: Alice & the Wave Band Pop Music Concert celebrating Asian American and Native Hawaiian/Pacific Islander Heritage Month (AANHPI). This free event takes place on Sunday, May 31, 2026, from 1:30 PM to 3:45 PM at the San Francisco Public Library (100 Larkin St, San Francisco, CA 94102) in the Lower Level/Koret Auditorium. The event features two parts: 1:30-2:00 PM includes piano and violin performances by youth from Rhymes Star Learning at the Koret Foyer, followed by 2:15-3:45 PM with the full Alice & the Wave Band concert. The band, rated "Sensational Band of the Orient" by Bay Area FM 96.5 KOIT radio, is known for their diverse musical style and performed at the 2023 APEC Reception & Gala. The event is free with no RSVP required. Attendees can expect an engaging multicultural musical experience featuring various genres and multilingual performances. This is a partnership between Global Chinese Pop Music Association, Rhymes Star Learning, and the Chinese Center of San Francisco Public Library.

events.title: Live Stream Author Talk: George Takei
events.description: To close out the celebration of One Book, One Coast, we will be live streaming an author talk at all our library locations with George Takei, the author of this year's highlighted book, 'They Called Us Enemy.'
events.event_detail: The event is a live stream author talk featuring George Takei, the actor known as Hikaru Sulu from Star Trek and author of the graphic memoir "They Called Us Enemy." The event takes place on Sunday from 2:00 PM to 4:00 PM, originating from Los Altos Library but available via live stream at all Santa Clara County Library locations. Attendees can expect an interview with George Takei conducted by Dr. Skye Patrick and Cathy De Leon, discussing his childhood imprisonment in American incarceration camps during World War II, his experiences as a Japanese American, and his journey as an actor, author, and equal rights advocate. The event is part of the One Book, One Coast collaborative reading program and celebrates Asian American Native Hawaiian Pacific Islander Heritage Month. It is suitable for adults and explores themes of patriotism, family, loyalty, and what it means to be American. ASL accessibility accommodations are available with advance notice.

events.event_detail: One Book, One Coast (OBOC) is a multi-state community reading initiative featuring George Takei's graphic memoir 'They Called Us Enemy,' recounting his childhood experience of incarceration alongside 120,000+ Japanese Americans following Executive Order 9066 in 1942. This virtual livestream event runs from 2:00 PM to 4:00 PM and is suitable for Adults, Teens, and Families. Attendees can register to view the livestream from anywhere. The event celebrates Asian American and Pacific Islander Heritage Month and serves as a book club discussion.

Attendees can expect to chat with new people about interesting topics in a friendly group setting. Each discussion features new topics and vocabulary to practice, and discussion leaders can help with pronunciation. The event is part of the library's Education and Literacy programs. The event takes place from 2:00 PM to 4:00 PM as part of the One Book, One Coast initiative, a multi-state community reading program spanning from California's southern border to Washington state. Takei reflects on his childhood experience in U.S. incarceration camps during World War II following Executive Order 9066, discussing the lasting impact of this history today. Attendees can expect an engaging conversation about Japanese American history, personal reflection, and the importance of remembering this period. Registration is required via Zoom. events.title: Herstory Exhibit: The Legal History of Chinese American Women
events.description: Invisible No More: Chinese American Women Shaping American Law. From the landmark 1874 Supreme Court case involving Chinese women to today's generation of judges and elected officials.
events.event_detail: Herstory Exhibit: The Legal History of Chinese American Women is a special exhibit celebrating Chinese American women who shaped U.S. law against significant odds. From the landmark 1874 Supreme Court case involving Chinese women to today's generation of judges and elected officials, this exhibit highlights everyday individuals who stood up for their rights and redefined the American story. Visitors will discover how Chinese American women influenced U.S. law, why their stories were nearly erased, the growing presence of women in the judiciary and public life, and the power of visibility in advancing justice. The exhibit runs May 2 - May 31, 2026, and is available for viewing during regular library hours at the Dublin Library. Curated by Dr. Chang C. Chen, a California attorney whose Herstory series is collected by the Library of Congress and exhibited in over 80 institutions. This is a self-guided viewing experience suitable for everyone. Library staff may be present for photos; notify them if you prefer not to be recorded.

events.title: The Library Wellness Team
events.description: Contra Costa County Health Services in partnership with Contra Costa County Library System are here to support library staff and patrons alike. Currently the Library Wellness Team consists of a Community Support Worker and Mental Health Professional.
events.event_detail: The Library Wellness Team is a partnership between Contra Costa County Health Services and the Contra Costa County Library System. The team includes a Community Support Worker and Mental Health Clinician who assist library patrons with various needs that library staff may not be able to address. They provide education about Contra Costa County's mental health and community support services, offering a supportive ear and connections to resources. The event occurs on Monday, June 1, 2026, from 10:00am to 4:00pm at the Concord Library (2900 Salvio Street, Concord, CA 94519). The Wellness Team rotates through multiple library locations throughout the week. Attendees can expect to receive information about mental health resources, community support services, and have the opportunity to speak with trained professionals in a supportive, judgment-free environment.

events.title: Veterans' In Person Services
events.description: Our Veterans Service Representatives (VSR's) are thoroughly trained and accredited by the United States Department of Veterans Affairs to represent you. Contra Costa County VSR's are not employees of the federal government, they are county employees.
events.event_detail: Veterans' In Person Services event held at the Brentwood library branch on Monday, June 1, 2026, from 10:00am to 4:00pm. Veterans Service Representatives (VSR's) who are trained and accredited by the United States Department of Veterans Affairs will assist veterans with securing maximum benefits. They can help with compensation for service-related disabilities, pension for wartime Veterans, education benefits, vocational rehabilitation, medical treatment at VA Medical Centers, home loan benefits, government life insurance, burial benefits, military survivor benefits, and the California College Tuition Fee Waiver Program. Representatives work closely with service officers from Veterans organizations. Appointments are required. The event takes place upstairs in the Programs Room at 104 Oak Street, Brentwood, California 94513.

events.title: Family Resource Navigators
events.description: Family Resource Navigators is a Community Based organization that supports families when faced with a new disability or special health care diagnosis for their child.
events.event_detail: Family Resource Navigators is a community-based organization that supports families facing a new disability or special health care diagnosis for their child. This event takes place in the Main Children's Room at Oakland Public Library from 10:00 AM to 11:30 AM. Attendees can learn about FRN's services and chat with them in person. The organization helps families navigate new diagnoses, provides emotional support, assists with transition to adulthood for young adults with disabilities, and helps families navigate complex systems like IEPs and therapies. They offer guidance on available options for continued education, independence, and job readiness. FRN serves families who live or work in the East Bay. For more information, call the Warmline at 510-547-7322. Suitable for adults, kids, and teens.

events.title: Tai Chi
events.description: Chen-style Taijiquan (Tai Chi) is widely acknowledged as the ancestor of all other styles of Taijiquan. This class will introduce the Chen-style Taijiquan form, Silk-reeling Exercises and Wuji Qigong.
events.event_detail: Chen-style Taijiquan (Tai Chi) class offered by San Mateo County Libraries at the Foster City branch. This event introduces Chen-style Taijiquan form, Silk-reeling Exercises, and Wuji Qigong (standing meditation). The Chen-style form is soft and graceful with strong rooted stands that help students develop strength, balance, coordination, and an understanding of basic Taiji principles. Silk-reeling Exercises are spiral movements that promote muscle relaxation and flexibility by reducing physical tension. Wuji Qigong helps cultivate internal energy (qi) through proper body alignment, improving energy flow and enhancing immune systems while reducing physical and mental stress. Suitable for adults 19+ and adults 55+. Space is limited and admission is first-come, first-served. No registration required.

events.title: Tai Chi
events.description: What is T'ai-chi? T'ai-chi Ch'uan is an ancient Chinese art which combines meditation in movement and healthful exercise. The training includes the practice of a 37 posture form which teaches relaxation, balance and strength.
events.event_detail: Tai Chi class at Walnut Creek Library on Monday, June 1, 2026 from 10:15am to 11:15am in the Oak View Room upstairs. This is an ancient Chinese art combining meditation in movement and healthful exercise, teaching a 37 posture form developed by Professor Cheng Man-ching from the Yang system. The class focuses on relaxation, balance and strength, plus a partner practice building sensitivity and timing. No prior training is needed; everyone with interest is welcome. Medical research demonstrates benefits including reduced incidence of falls, increased relaxation, calmness, flexibility and balance. Participants will learn basic Tai Chi movements that look like slow motion dance. Regular attendance is recommended to realize the benefits.

This family-friendly event is suitable for preschoolers (ages 0-5) and children (ages 6-11). Attendees can expect an entertaining and educational performance that celebrates African American culture and the Juneteenth holiday through comedy, juggling, and rhythmic body percussion. The show encourages active participation from the audience, making it an engaging experience for the whole family.

events.title: Qigong
events.description: Qigong means practice of vital energy. In this class, we will practice a series of gentle spiral movements that help to open all the major joints.
events.event_detail: Qigong is a free wellness class offered by San Mateo County Libraries at the San Carlos Adult Community Center (601 Chestnut Street). The class runs from 10:30 AM to 11:30 AM. Qigong means "practice of vital energy" and involves gentle spiral movements designed to open all major joints in the body and increase internal energy flow. The practice promotes better flexibility and mobility while reducing tension and strain. This class is suitable for adults (19+) and is also 55+ friendly. Participants should wear comfortable, loose-fitting clothing that allows for easy movement. No prior experience with Qigong is required to attend.

Designed for babies from newborns up to 18 months old, the program features nursery rhymes and songs that parents and caregivers can do together with their little ones to support early development. The event runs every Monday from 12:00 PM to 1:30 PM at the Newark Branch of Alameda County Library. Participants receive free learning materials to support their English conversation skill development. This is a casual, welcoming environment where attendees can practice speaking, listening, and conversation skills with others. The group is suitable for adults looking to improve their English proficiency in a supportive, low-pressure setting. Library staff may be present and could take photos or recordings during the event.

events.title: Opening: The Biggest Small Works Show 2026
events.description: Call for Entry: 2D and Wall Mounted 3D. Small work exhibit. Presented by Gallery Sausalito.
events.event_detail: Opening reception for The Biggest Small Works Show 2026 at Gallery Sausalito. This is the third annual exhibition featuring small artwork in all mediums, with this year's theme being SWEET. The exhibition runs from June 1-25, 2026, with the opening reception on the first Saturday in June. Attendees can view artwork from approximately 74 artists displayed in the gallery, meet the artists, and enjoy the reception. Gallery hours are Thursday through Monday, 12:00 pm - 6:00 pm. The venue is located at 30 Princess Street in Sausalito. Artists are encouraged to attend and bring friends to this community art event.

Lunch is distributed in the library lobby from 12:30 PM to 1:30 PM while supplies last. Children and teens must be present to receive their own meal. The program aims to provide nutritious meals to youth during summer break when school lunch programs are unavailable. No registration or proof of income is required to participate.

events.title: Book Group

events.event_detail: Book Group is a monthly book discussion event held at the Woodside library branch of San Mateo County Libraries. The group meets on the first Monday of each month from 1:00 PM to 2:00 PM to discuss select fiction and non-fiction books. If the first Monday falls on a holiday, the meeting moves to the second Monday. This event is suitable for adults (19+) and conducted in English. Attendees can expect a lively discussion with other book lovers, sharing insights and perspectives on the selected reading material.

The session focuses on a combination of movement, meditation, and breathing exercises designed for stress relief, relaxation, and mind-body connection. All skill levels are welcome. Participants are asked to bring their own towel or mat. This health and wellness event is suitable for adults 19+ and is also 55+ friendly.

events.title: Friends of the Millbrae Library Book Club

events.event_detail: Friends of the Millbrae Library Book Club is a monthly book discussion group that meets on the first Monday of every month from 1:00 PM to 2:00 PM at the Millbrae Library. This is an ongoing, casual discussion of works of all forms and genres, welcoming both casual and avid readers. Attendees discuss the month's chosen book. The event is suitable for adults (19+) and is conducted in English. No registration is required to attend.

events.event_detail: The Reptile Show with East Bay Vivarium is a free family event taking place at the Eastmont Branch of the Oakland Public Library on Monday, June 1, 2026 from 1:00 pm to 2:00 pm. Experts from the East Bay Vivarium will bring their reptiles, amphibians, and bugs to share with attendees. Children and families can meet scaly friends up close and learn about the fascinating world of reptiles through this interactive educational presentation. The event is suitable for toddlers, preschoolers, and grade schoolers. No registration is required, and admission is free.

events.title: East Bay Vivarium

This educational program teaches about the fascinating world of cold-blooded creatures and insects. The event runs from 1:00 PM to 2:00 PM and is part of the OPL Summer program. Suitable for kids of all ages, grade schoolers, tweens, toddlers, preschoolers, and families. Attendees can expect to meet some scaly friends up close, learn interesting facts about reptiles, and enjoy an engaging live animal presentation.

events.event_detail: SF's Conservatory of Flowers offers free admission on the first Tuesday of every month at Golden Gate Park. The historic greenhouse, opened in 1879, is the oldest existing conservatory of its kind in the Western Hemisphere. Visitors can explore nearly 2,000 species of rare, exotic, and endangered plants from more than 50 countries. Hours are 10am-4:30pm (last entry at 4pm). Admission is normally $12 for non-SF residents, but free for everyone on free days. The venue also offers additional free or reduced admission through Museums for All for San Francisco residents on public benefits, plus free admission for Military, Veterans, and children 4 and under. A winter light show called Photosynthesis is also available free every night.

events.event_detail: Toddler Storytime is a free library program featuring songs, active rhymes, and stories designed for children ages 18 months to 3 years. The event takes place every Tuesday at 10:15am at the Piedmont Ave. Branch of Oakland Public Library (80 Echo Avenue, Oakland, CA). Each session runs from 10:15am to 10:30am, followed by optional stay-and-play time with age-appropriate toys until 11:15am. Weather permitting, storytime may be held outside the library building. Patrons are asked to refrain from wearing scented products. This is a free community event perfect for toddlers and their caregivers.

events.title: SF's Cartoon Art Museum's Pay What You Wish Day (First Tuesdays)
events.description: Pay What You Wish Day
events.event_detail: Cartoon Art Museum's Pay What You Wish Day is a monthly event held on the first Tuesday of every month from 11:00 am to 5:00 pm at the Cartoon Art Museum located at 781 Beach Street in San Francisco, near Fisherman's Wharf. Founded in 1984, the museum houses approximately 7,000 original pieces of cartoon art in its permanent collection, including comic strips, comic books, anime, political cartoons, graphic novels, and underground comix. On Pay What You Wish Days, visitors set their own admission price, making it accessible for all. Attendees can view original cartoon art exhibitions and screenings, explore the reading room, participate in family-oriented activities in the kids corner, and learn about cartoon art history and its role in society. The museum also has a store and library for visitors to enjoy.

events.description: Free lunchtime concert series
events.event_detail: SF's free lunchtime concert series Civic Center Soundtrack returns for its third season, running every Tuesday and Thursday from 12 pm to 3 pm from April 14 through October 2026. The event takes place at Fulton Plaza outside the San Francisco Public Library in the Civic Center neighborhood. Each day features three performers spanning a mix of musical genres and local talent. New for 2026, rotating food trucks join the festivities, creating a lively midday hangout. Attendees can bring their own lunch or purchase food from trucks while enjoying free live outdoor music. The event is free to attend and open to downtown workers, residents, families, and anyone looking for an affordable midday break with live entertainment.

events.title: Sprout Pop Up!
events.event_detail: Sprout Pop Up! is a free gardening event at Oakland Public Library's Golden Gate Branch. Come pick up free sprouts for your garden! The event runs from 1:00 PM to 3:00 PM and offers a variety of flower, herb, fruit, and vegetable sprouts. Sprouts come from the Golden Gate branch's seed library and from library patrons who have grown their plants to seed and donated them. Library staff cares for the sprouts near the seed library inside the branch for easy access. Supplies are limited and available on a first-come-first-serve basis. This event is suitable for adults, teens, and families interested in gardening. For information about available sprout types, call Golden Gate library at 510-597-5023.

events.description: Come join us at the Novato Library to practice your Spanish language speaking skills. Be part of this free weekly program. At every class there will be a leading tutor from the Novato Library and assisting tutors to help participants practice their Spanish.

The event takes place every week from 4:00 PM to 5:30 PM at the Novato branch of the Marin County Free Library. Trained tutors lead each session to help participants improve their conversation abilities. No registration is required to attend, making it accessible to anyone interested in practicing Spanish. The program welcomes all skill levels and provides a supportive environment for language practice.

events.title: Online Resource
events.event_detail: Santa Clara County Library District provides free online resources and library services to the community. Available 24/7 through their online portal, users can access eBooks, audiobooks, eMagazines, movies, music, language learning (70+ languages including ASL), meditation tools like Headspace, research databases, career resources, test prep, coding tutorials, and more. The library system serves multiple cities including Campbell, Cupertino, Gilroy, Los Altos, Milpitas, Morgan Hill, Saratoga, and Woodland. Virtual author talks and online tutoring are also offered. No specific time or venue - available anytime online with a library card.

events.title: SF's Free Arcade Game Night at The Detour (First Tuesdays)
events.description: Free unlimited play wristband with any purchase from bar
events.event_detail: SF's Free Arcade Game Night at The Detour (Free Play Tuesday) is a monthly event held on the first Tuesday of every month from 4pm until midnight. The venue is The Detour SF located at 2200 Market St #A in San Francisco's Castro neighborhood. Attendees receive a free unlimited play wristband with any purchase from the bar, granting access to over 40 arcade video games and two featured pinball machines. Games include classics like Time Crisis 2, The Simpsons, Killer Queen, Buck Hunter HD Wild, Ms. Pac Man, Mortal Kombat 3, and pinball machines such as The Addams Family, Game of Thrones, and The Mandalorian. The venue also features a full bar serving craft beer and cocktails, plus Pan Pacific Asian street food. Happy hour runs 4-6pm with discounted drinks. Proof of vaccination is required for indoor entry, and masks are required when not actively eating or drinking.

events.title: South Beach Coastal Resilience Project Open House
events.description: Almost full - Community open house event
events.event_detail: South Beach Coastal Resilience Project Open House hosted by the Port of San Francisco. This community open house takes place on Tuesday, June 2 from 5:30 PM to 7:30 PM at the Ferry Building Grand Hall (Second Floor), San Francisco, CA 94105. Attendees will learn about the South Beach Coastal Resilience Project which aims to advance waterfront resilience along the Embarcadero between Harrison and Townsend Streets. The project addresses seismic risks in one of the oldest wharf areas and supports major developments at Pier 30/32 and Pier 38/40. The project will deliver earthquake-stable seawall and wharves while enhancing the public promenade for recreation and mobility. This is an opportunity for community members to learn about the project, view plans and displays, and provide their input. The event is free and family-friendly, lasting approximately 2 hours. Refreshments may be available.

The project will support developments at Pier 30/32 and Pier 38/40 while delivering earthquake-stable seawall and wharves and enhancing the public promenade for recreation and mobility. Attendees can expect to learn about project details, view displays, and provide their input on the plans. The event takes place on Tuesday, June 2 from 5:30 PM to 7:30 PM at the Ferry Building Grand Hall, Second Floor in San Francisco. The event is 2 hours and in person.

Attendees can expect to learn about volunteer opportunities, meet library staff, and sign up for volunteer positions. Multiple orientation sessions are available: Saturday 5/16/26 from 2-3pm, Tuesday 5/19/26 from 6-7pm, Tuesday 6/2/26 from 6-7pm, and Saturday 6/6/26 from 2-3pm. The event is suitable for teens and focuses on leadership development through community service. Teens will have the opportunity to make friends, serve their community, and work with other youth. No registration appears to be required based on the event page.

events.title: The Black Studies Collective Community Reading and Discussion Series
events.description: The West Oakland Branch Library is excited to announce that the Black Studies Collective is back! This series invites community members to reflect on how the ideas and traditions of Black Studies continue to shape our communities.
events.event_detail: The Black Studies Collective Community Reading and Discussion Series is a four-part book discussion series hosted at the West Oakland Branch Library. The second cohort is reading 'The Black Antifascist Tradition: Fighting Back From Anti-Lynching to Abolition' by Jeanelle K. Hope and Bill Mullen. An orientation session takes place on Tuesday, June 2, 2026 from 6:00-7:15 PM. The monthly discussion meetings then continue on the first Tuesday of each month from July through October 2026, also from 6:00-7:15 PM. Participants can pick up reading materials at orientation, and a limited number of books are available for distribution. This small, discussion-based group encourages attendees to participate in at least 3 of the 4 sessions. Registration is required (in person or by phone). The series celebrates Black Studies as a living, community-centered tradition and continues West Oakland's legacy of collective learning and cultural engagement. Suitable for adults.

events.title: 2026 Summer Reading Program: Learning Chinese language and culture
events.description: Join us for an interactive program designed to help participants learn basic Chinese language skills and develop an appreciation for Chinese culture through fun and engaging activities. All materials will be provided.
events.event_detail: A free 4-week Chinese language and culture learning program for adults held at Campbell Library. The program runs June 2-27, 2026, with sessions twice per week: Tuesdays and Wednesdays from 6:30-8:30 PM, and Saturdays from 10:30 AM-12:30 PM. Participants must commit to attending all sessions. The program teaches basic Chinese language skills and Chinese culture appreciation through fun, interactive activities. All materials are provided. Classes are taught by Linda Chen, a Mandarin teacher at Branham High School with over 20 years of experience. This is a partnership between TECO (Education Division of the Taipei Economic Cultural Office) and Campbell Library. Registration is required, and space is limited.

events.title: Oakland's Mezcal & Mole Comedy Night (Mondays & Tuesdays)
events.description: Pop-up live comedy shows at unique spots
events.event_detail: Oakland's Mezcal & Mole Comedy Night is a weekly live comedy show hosted by HellaFunny at Mesa Maguey, an upscale agave bar and Oaxacan restaurant in the Temescal neighborhood. The event takes place every Monday and Tuesday at 7pm, featuring a 70+ minute show with 4-5 professional comedians who have credits from venues like Cobbs, Punchline, SF Sketchfest, and ABC/NBC. Admission is free with RSVP (first 50 people get in free), though food and drinks are available for purchase. The venue offers delicious Oaxacan dishes including mole, tacos, enchiladas, and ceviche, with most plates around $20. It's described as a perfect date-night spot with a welcoming dining room and bar atmosphere. The address is 4031 Broadway, Oakland, CA.

events.title: FREE: SF's Laugh GPT AI-Powered Comedy Night (The Function)
events.description: RSVP Required
events.event_detail: Laugh GPT is an AI-powered comedy show held every Tuesday at The Function, a black-owned comedy club in San Francisco's Mid Market/Hayes Valley area. Shows run from 7:30pm to 9:00pm, featuring 4-5 comedians who use AI assistance to craft and deliver jokes. The event was recently featured in the Washington Post. Attendees can expect a 70-90 minute show with comics who have performed at venues like Cobbs, Punchline, SF Sketchfest, Clusterfest, and Outside Lands. The show is free with RSVP (first 50 people get free tickets), though donations are appreciated and there is a two-drink minimum to support the bar. Arrive early to enjoy happy hour from 5-7pm before the show. The club features colorful murals, cozy seating, and an electric atmosphere where audiences help determine whether humans or AI are funnier.

events.description: No admission charge
events.event_detail: Disco Taco Tuesday at Underdogs Cantina is a weekly nightlife event held every Tuesday from 7:30pm to 10:00pm at 128 King St. in San Francisco's SoMa neighborhood (across from the ballpark). The main draw is $1 margaritas available from 7:30pm to 8:00pm, with happy hour prices all night long. The venue features 25+ TVs for sports viewing, arcade games for entertainment, and a capacity of 300+ people. There's no cover charge for admission. Attendees can enjoy discounted drinks, tacos, and a lively bar atmosphere with disco-themed entertainment. It's a great option for affordable nightlife in SF, particularly during baseball season due to its proximity to the ballpark.

events.event_detail: First Tuesdays Free Comedy Showcase & Happy Hour is a free comedy event held on the first Tuesday of each month at The Layover, 1517 Franklin Street in Oakland. Shows run from 8pm to 10pm and feature professional comedians who have appeared on HBO, Showtime, Comedy Central, and late night TV. Happy hour drink specials are available until show time. Free admission with RSVP required. Hosted by Lyall Behrens, Francesca Fiorentini, and Josef Anolin, this monthly event offers a fun night out with top comedians and drink specials in a bar venue setting.

The event features free dance lessons and free admission, making it accessible for beginners and experienced dancers alike. Located at 2045 Mt. Diablo Street in downtown Concord, the venue is one block from Todos Santos Park. Attendees can take BART to the Concord BART station for easy access, or drive and park for free in the Salvio Street garage. Vinnies Bar & Grill offers food and drinks for purchase. Country line dancing is the main activity, with a welcoming atmosphere for dancers of all skill levels. The recurring event runs throughout the summer and fall months with dates listed through late November.

This is a socially-distant, old-fashioned outdoor movie experience where you watch from your car. Regular pricing is $9 for adults and $2 for kids ages 5-11, with kids 4 and under free.

events.title: Japanese Tea Garden Free Admission Hour (Golden Gate Park)
events.description: Free from 9-10am on Monday, Wednesday and Friday
events.event_detail: Japanese Tea Garden's Free Admission Hour at Golden Gate Park in San Francisco. Free entry for everyone (including non-residents) from 9-10 am every Monday, Wednesday, and Friday. San Francisco residents with valid ID get free admission all other times. The garden features classic Japanese elements including an arched drum bridge, pagodas, stone lanterns, stepping stone paths, koi ponds, zen garden, and native Japanese plants. Cherry blossom trees bloom in March and April. Regular non-resident admission is $12-16 depending on season. Located at 75 Hagiwara Tea Garden Dr, Golden Gate Park. Open daily starting at 9am with last entry 30 minutes before closing. Visitors can explore the serene garden paths, view koi ponds, take photos, and enjoy the tranquil atmosphere.

SF Zoo Free Admission Day (June 2026)
events.description: Free admission offer only valid to San Francisco residents with valid ID
events.event_detail: The San Francisco Zoo offers free admission for San Francisco residents on specific days, typically the first or second Wednesday of each month. On June 3, 2026, from 10am to 5pm (last entry at 4pm), SF residents with valid ID can enjoy Northern California's largest zoological park featuring 250 animal species in naturalistic settings. The zoo is located on Sloat Blvd. and The Great Highway near the Pacific Ocean. Attendees can explore various animal exhibits, watch keeper talks, and enjoy the outdoor park setting. Free admission is subject to capacity. Residents must bring valid photo ID or a utility bill with their name and address. Parking in the main lot is $13, but free street parking is available along Sloat Blvd.

events.title: Wee Play: Drop-In Playtime
events.description: Wee Play drop-in playtime, 10am-1pm
events.event_detail: Alameda's Wee Play is a drop-in playtime program for children 6 months to 3 years old, requiring caregiver supervision. Held at Room 120 in the Alameda Veterans Memorial Building at 2203 Central Avenue, the sessions run from 10:00 am to 1:00 pm on multiple days throughout the week (Mondays, Wednesdays, Thursdays, and Fridays). Each session features developmental and exploratory play activities that are minimally structured, allowing children to explore at their own pace. Daily themes include arts & crafts, STEM/numbers/reading, and creative play/dance/music. The program costs $6 per child (daily fee at the door). Registration is encouraged for the first visit. Children must be accompanied by a parent or caregiver at all times. Volunteers can earn free entrance by assisting with setup/cleanup.

events.description: Join Ms. Amanda every Wednesday morning for a wiggly, giggly, all-ages, multilingual storytime! We'll read books, sing songs, share imaginative play, and learn something new every day. Open to ages 0-5 and caregivers.
events.event_detail: Wiggles and Wonder Storytime is a weekly storytime program for young children (ages 0-5) and their caregivers, held at the Marin City branch of Marin County Free Library. The event takes place every Wednesday from 10:15 AM to 11:00 AM. Led by Ms. Amanda, the program features reading books, singing songs, imaginative play, and learning activities. This multilingual storytime welcomes all ages and families. Note: The program ends for the year on December 17 and returns February 25.

events.title: Storytime on the Lawn
events.description: Storytime on the Lawn, 10:30am
events.event_detail: Storytime on the Lawn is a free outdoor storytime event hosted by the North Branch of the Berkeley Public Library. The event features stories, songs, rhymes, and fun activities for children ages 2-5, lasting approximately 30 minutes. It takes place weather permitting on the lawn at the North Branch library located at 1170 The Alameda in Berkeley. The event runs every Wednesday from April 8 through June 3, 2026, from 10:30 am to 11:00 am. Attendees are encouraged to bring a blanket or mat to sit on. After the storytime concludes, children can stay for playtime with toys, soft blocks, and musical instruments, providing an opportunity for social interaction with other caregivers. The event is free to attend, and more information is available by calling 510-981-6250.

events.event_detail: Baby & Me is a free lap-sit program for infants through 2 years old and their caregivers. The event features songs, nursery rhymes, knee-bounces, and movement activities designed to develop pre-literacy skills. The venue is 21+ and attendees should arrive 20-30 minutes early to check in. This event is part of HellaFunny's programming showcasing People of Color comedians in a welcoming bar environment.

events.title: FREE Hecklers Welcome SF's First Stand-Up Comedy Show That Invites Heckling
events.description: Free with RSVP
events.event_detail: Hecklers Welcome is San Francisco's first stand-up comedy show that encourages audience heckling and participation. The show takes place every Thursday from 7:30 PM to 9:00 PM at The Function venue, located at 1414 Market Street in the Mid Market area of San Francisco. The event features 4-5 professional comedians from venues like Cobb's, Punch Line, and SF Sketchfest, performing in a fast-paced 70-90 minute show. Audience members are invited to talk back, roast performers, and challenge the comics. First 50 RSVPs enter free, otherwise $20 at the door. The venue has a two-drink minimum. Lineups change weekly, and donations are welcome.

events.title: 16th & Mission Open Mic (w/out a mic)
events.description: Absolutely free for all!
events.event_detail: 16th & Mission Open Mic (w/out a mic) is a free weekly outdoor open mic event held every Thursday from 9pm to midnight at the southwest streetcorner of 16th & Mission BART station in San Francisco. Celebrating nearly 20 years, this inclusive event welcomes poets, musicians, emcees, comedians, and all forms of artistic expression in any language. The venue is outdoors amidst pigeons under the stars. Absolutely free for all attendees, no registration required. Whether you want to perform or watch, come support your local streetcorner community and enjoy the authentic San Francisco open mic experience.

events.title: Arcade Karaoke: SF's Wild New Thursday Night Party + $3 Shots (SF)
events.description: Free with RSVP. - 21+
events.event_detail: Arcade Karaoke is a wild Thursday night party held at The Function venue, located at 1414 Market Street in San Francisco's Mid Market area. The event runs every Thursday from 9pm until 2am. Attendees can expect live band karaoke with guitars, drums, piano, and over 1000 songs. The evening features Guitar Hero tournaments, arcade games like Super Smash Bros, Grand Theft Auto, and Mario Kart on giant projectors. Hosted by MC Dirty Murty, the event includes immersive lighting effects and an AI Rockstar Robot drummer. Happy Hour deals run all night with Crazy Hour offering $3 shots every hour on the hour. A VIP Rockstar Pass is available for $10 for faster stage access and priority seating. Free admission with RSVP, 21+ only. Two drink minimum applies to support bar staff.

events.title: Every Thursday: Inner Circle Dance Party at White Rabbit (SF)
events.description: Inner Circle is always Free with RSVP
events.event_detail: Inner Circle is a free weekly dance party held every Thursday from 9pm to 1am at White Rabbit (3138 Fillmore St., San Francisco). The event features guest DJs spinning House, Disco, Remixes, Currents, Classics and more. It's a long-running Thursday night tradition celebrating dance music culture with no cover charge. Attendees can expect an energetic atmosphere dedicated to DJ culture and dance music, featuring fresh lineup of guest DJs who bring unique energy to every set. The venue has two rooms and two bars. Free admission with RSVP. The party runs ongoing through January 1st.

events.title: Sadderday: An Emo/Pop-Punk/Screamo Dance Party | SF
events.description: Dance party
events.event_detail: Sadderday is a recurring dance party celebrating the emo, pop-punk, and screamo era. Held every first Thursday of the month at 9:30 pm at Pop's Bar in San Francisco's Mission District, this free event invites attendees to relive the nostalgia of white belts, MySpace profiles, and dramatic bangs. The dance floor stays packed all night spinning emo, pop punk, post-hardcore, screamo, indie, electro, and 90s/2000s hits. Partygoers can expect an energetic atmosphere with like-minded fans ready to dance, sing along, and embrace their early 2000s alter egos. The venue is located at 2800 24th St, San Francisco, CA 94110. No cover charge makes this an affordable night out for anyone looking to unleash their inner emo.

events.description: FREE ENTRY ALL NIGHT
events.event_detail: Free Karaoke Night Every Thursday at Bottom's Up bar. This recurring event offers free entry all night and runs every Thursday from 10PM to 2AM. The venue is located at 4704 Mission St., San Francisco, CA 94112 in the Mission District. Attendees can expect a night of singing and fun with karaoke from late night into the early morning hours. The event is 21+ only. No cover charge, making it an accessible and budget-friendly way to enjoy karaoke in San Francisco.

events.title: Pop-N-Play
events.description: Pop-N-Play drop-in playtime, 9am-12pm
events.event_detail: Pop-N-Play is an indoor play session held at Ruby's Tumbling in Alameda. The event runs on Mondays, Wednesdays, and Fridays from 9am to 12pm, with select dates throughout spring and early summer 2026. Children can come and play in the tumbling gym, with options for parents to stay with their child ($15 per child) or drop off ($35). Siblings receive a $10 discount. Monthly drop-off packages are available for $370. Payment is cash only. The event is suitable for toddlers through grade schoolers. Kids can enjoy open play time in a gym environment with tumbling equipment and play structures.

events.title: Explore Blake Garden
events.description: Explore Blake Garden - free admission, 9am-4pm
events.event_detail: Explore Blake Garden is a free self-guided visit to a 10.6-acre public garden in Kensington with stunning hill views of the San Francisco Bay and Golden Gate Bridge. The garden features native plants, a reflection pool, flower garden, and a Create-with-Nature Zone for kids. Blake Garden is open Tuesdays through Fridays from 9 AM to 4 PM, closed on Mondays, weekends, and University holidays. Parking is free. The event recurs on select dates in 2026 (April through June). Visitors can explore at their own pace, enjoy the views, and let children play in the nature zone.

events.title: Wee Play: Drop-In Playtime
events.description: Wee Play drop-in playtime, 10am-1pm
events.event_detail: Wee Play is a drop-in playtime program for children 6 months to 3 years old, held at the Alameda Veterans Memorial Building (Room 120) at 2203 Central Avenue in Alameda, CA. Activities include developmental and exploratory play that is minimally structured, allowing children to explore on their own terms. Each day features a special focus such as arts & crafts, STEM/numbers/reading, or creative play/dance/music. Children must be accompanied by a parent or caregiver at all times. The event runs from 10:00 am to 1:00 pm on select dates throughout April-June 2026. Registration is encouraged online prior to first visit to add your child to the roster, though paper forms are available. Free to register, but $6 daily fee per child is collected at the door. Volunteers who assist with setup/cleanup receive free entrance. Closed on holidays including Memorial Day, Juneteenth, Independence Day, Labor Day, and more.

events.title: Dance, Dance, Dance Party
events.description: Dance, Dance, Dance Party, 10:30am
events.event_detail: Dance, Dance, Dance Party is a family-friendly dance event held at the Berkeley Public Library Central Branch. DJ AvoColey plays music while Children's Librarians lead storytime and teach dances from the 80s and 90s. Week one features an 80s Dance Party at 10:30am, and week two offers a 90s Dance Party at 3:30pm. This free event is part of the Plant a Seed, Read summer reading program. Kids are encouraged to bring their adults for a fun morning of music, movement, and stories. The event runs from 10:30am to 11:00am on Friday, June 5, 2026. All ages welcome.

events.title: Bicycle Safety Fair
events.description: Join us for a Bicycle Safety Fair! Learn about bike safety, proper helmet fitting, and road rules for cyclists. Fun activities for the whole family.
events.event_detail: The Bicycle Safety Fair is a community event hosted by the City of Napa during National Bicycle Safety Month. This family-friendly event teaches local youth and community members essential bicycle safety skills through hands-on activities. Attendees can participate in a Bike Rodeo that teaches the rules of the road in a safe and fun riding course. Participants can bring their own bike or borrow one provided at the event. The fair features safety instruction from certified bicycle safety instructors and local partners including the Napa County Bicycle Coalition and CHP Bicycle Patrol. Activities may include a neighborhood ride following the safety demonstrations. The event is free and open to all ages, promoting safe cycling practices for both bicyclists and drivers.

events.event_detail: Summer Fridays is a weekly Friday evening series running from May 15 through June 2026 at Epicurious Garden, located at 1511 Shattuck Avenue in North Berkeley. From 5 to 8pm, families can enjoy live music performances on the back garden patio and upper terrace while dining on food from Hopscotch Chicken or Itani Sushi. Each week from 5 to 7pm, Happily Ever Laughter provides children's entertainment with costumed fairytale characters performing roaming table-side activities like face painting, balloon twisting, magic shows, and movement games. The schedule rotates different musicians and characters weekly, giving families a fresh experience each visit. No tickets or reservations are required. This is a free event with food available for purchase. The patio setting offers ample open seating, making it an ideal outdoor dining experience for families with children of all ages.

The event is held at a local park or community center, providing a fun and affordable entertainment option for families with children. Attendees should bring blankets or lawn chairs for comfortable seating. Concessions may be available for purchase, or families can bring their own snacks and beverages.

events.title: MUSIC & MARKET
events.description: When summer hits Todos Santos Plaza, Thursdays come alive in the best way possible. From June 4 through September 25, Thursday nights have a standing date. The Farmers' Market kicks things off at 4 p.m., then at 6:30 p.m., the music takes over, turning the plaza into an open-air dance floor under the sky. Free admission.
events.event_detail: Music & Market is a free weekly summer event held at Todos Santos Park in Downtown Concord. Every Thursday from June 4 through September 25, the plaza comes alive with the Farmers' Market starting at 4 p.m., featuring fresh produce, street food, and local vendors. At 6:30 p.m., live music takes over the outdoor space, running until 8 p.m. The event transforms the park into an open-air dance floor where attendees can enjoy performances, browse market stalls, and socialize with the community. It's a family-friendly gathering that captures the essence of summer evenings in Concord, combining good food, live entertainment, and a relaxed atmosphere. Bring your own lawn chair or blanket and enjoy Thursday nights with neighbors and friends under the summer sky.
